title: The left-derived coefficient path is the specified inverse pull comparison
statement: Let a:R→S be a morphism of commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] such that scalar extension along a_Z is exact for every scheme Z. For any scheme morphism f:X→Y use the specified unbounded internal-module derived functors and adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-comparisons]. Let θ=coefficientScalarPathIso(a,f) be the left-derived ordinary inverse coefficient square of [lem-sfb-coefficient-scalar-tensor-realization], so θ:T_Y ⋙ P_S ≅ P_R ⋙ T_X. Then θ=(derivedPullIso(a,f))⁻¹ [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso], as natural isomorphisms. No tensor, projection, boundedness, properness or finite-type assertion is part of this result.

proof.text: Unfold the path in [lem-sfb-coefficient-scalar-tensor-realization]: it is the inverse composition comparison for scalar extension at Y and S-pullback, followed by the left-derived inverse ordinary pullIso, then the composition comparison for R-pullback and scalar extension at X. Each comparison satisfies its left-derived counit factorization. Pasting these equations gives the ordinary coefficient square after homotopy localization.

proof.text: The unit factorization derivedη_fac_app of each specified derived adjunction [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] identifies its unit followed by the left counit with the localized ordinary unit followed by the right unit. For the scalar adjunctions transport the right adjoint along rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory, using its unit-factorization equation. Naturality of units shows that these equations compose according to [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Ordinary conjugation identifies inverse pullIso with inverse comapLowerStarIso [def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso, def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso]; its unit relation passes to homotopy categories.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars preserves K-injectives [lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives]. Use the defining unit equations of rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso, rightDerivedFunctorNatIso and rightDerivedFunctorCompIso in the specified derivedComapLowerStarIso [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-comparisons]. The exact scalar restriction transport satisfies rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory_hom_fac. Pasting these equations shows that inverse derivedComapLowerStarIso satisfies the localized inverse ordinary restriction-square equation. This direct calculation of the defining comparisons needs no auxiliary composition-adjunction normalization theorem.

proof.text: Apply the previous unit normalizations to the composites on the two sides of the square. The left-counit equation of Step 1 and right-unit equation of Step 3 imply the conjugation unit equation on every localized homotopy object. Localization detects equality of natural transformations, and the derived adjunction Hom bijection detects equality of their components. Thus the left path is the inverse conjugate of inverse derivedComapLowerStarIso, which is exactly inverse derivedPullIso [def-sfb-derived-pull-iso, def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso]. No tensor or projection formula is used.

theorem coefficientScalarPathIso_eq_derivedPullIso_symm
    {R S : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}}
    [MonObj R] [IsCommMonObj R] [MonObj S] [IsCommMonObj S]
    (a : R ⟶ S) [IsMonHom a]
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, PreservesFiniteLimits (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap a Z))]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    coefficientScalarPathIso a f = (derivedPullIso a f).symm
